newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - May 7.
newsitem.headline: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - May 7.

text.p: Following are views on the direction of Philippine stocks on Wednesday and main factors likely to affect trading:

* Shares are likely to pursue their rally following the $3 1/4 rise to $57 5/8 of Philippine Long Distance Telephone Co in Wall Street, said Elline Salvatierra, analyst at Dharmala Securities Phils Inc.
* Profit-taking may set in once the index reaches the 2,800 resistance, said Noel Reyes, research head at Anscor-Hagedorn.
* Sun Hung Kai Securities said foreign investors are still wary of buying after last week's plunge in share prices.
* On Tuesday, the Philippine Stock Exchange composite index climbed for the second day in a row by 40.11 points, or 1.47 percent, closing at 2,776.53 points.
* The Dow Jones posted a second consecutive record at close on Tuesday rising 10.83 points to 7,225.32. PLDT's ADR posted a significant gain of $3 1/4 to $57 5/8.
* Megaworld Properties & Holdings Inc said its board had approved a one-for-three rights offer at four pesos per share.

* Movie producer Premiere Entertainment Productions Inc said its net loss for the first three months ended March 31 had narrowed to 1.94 million pesos from a loss of 2.05 million in the year-ago period.
* The Philippine Commercial International Bank (PCIBank) said its net income in the first quarter of the year reached 1.07 billion pesos, sharply higher than the year-ago 684.5 million.
* The Bureau of Treasury said the yield on the Philippine two-year treasury note rose to 12 percent from the previous month's 11.50.
* Oil exploration firm Sinophil Corp said its unaudited net income in the first quarter of the year was 20.44 million pesos.
* Union Bank said its net income from January to March rose to 300.2 million pesos from 258.6 million the previous year.
* Manila Electric Co said it planned to cut power rates for industrial users to lure back companies that had set up their own power generation facilities.
* Philippine Telegraph & Telephone Corp said revenues rose 28 percent to 493.9 million pesos during the three months ending March 31. The firm operates on a fiscal year beginning July 1.
* Philippine Central Bank governor Gabriel Singson said the country's financial sector remained sound and was not about to suffer the same fate as Thailand.
* The National Statistics Office said Philippine exports in March rose to $1.996 billion from $1.67 billion a year ago.
* Cash-strapped thrift bank Monte de Piedad Savings Bank will reopen on Thursday after the entry of the Keppel Group of Singapore.

* Manila Bulletin said with the exception of diesel, prices of petroleum products are likely to drop from a range of 22 centavos to 80 centavos per litre due to lower Singapore Posted Prices, the benchmark for domestic prices.
* Philippine Savings Bank said its first quarter profits rose to 122.7 million pesos, a 25 percent increase from the same period last year.
* The peso closed lower at 26.365 to the dollar vs 26.374
* The Philippine interbank call loan average rose a shade up to 11.5625 percent from 11.53125 percent.
